Question (common phrasing): Legal first name / last name
Rule / how to answer: Use legal name exactly as on your ID/EAD. Fix ALL-CAPS from resume parsing to Title Case.

Question (common phrasing): Preferred first name
Rule / how to answer: If there is a separate Preferred field, legal name goes in First/Last.

Question (common phrasing): Email / Phone
Rule / how to answer: One application email everywhere. Phone with country code (+1 …) often auto-sets the country picker.

Question (common phrasing): Street address / City / State / ZIP / Country
Rule / how to answer: Workday parsers usually leave Address Line 1 empty — fill it.

Question (common phrasing): LinkedIn URL
Rule / how to answer: Use the full https://www.linkedin.com/in/... form; some Workday tenants reject the short form and block the whole step.

Question (common phrasing): Website / Portfolio
Rule / how to answer: Optional. Only include if it supports this lane.

Question (common phrasing): Current or most recent employer / job title
Rule / how to answer: Must match the first role on your resume.

Question (common phrasing): Pronouns
Name pronunciation
Rule / how to answer: Leave blank if you have no saved answer; don't invent one.

Question (common phrasing): Are you legally authorized to work in the United States?
Will you now or in the future require visa sponsorship?
What they screen for: Sponsorship filter, sometimes a hard gate
Rule / how to answer: Answer truthfully. Some forms split NOW vs FUTURE into two questions — answer each literally.

Question (common phrasing): Will you NOW require sponsorship? / IN THE FUTURE?
Rule / how to answer: Answer each half literally (e.g. on OPT: now = No, future = Yes).

Question (common phrasing): Do you have an UNRESTRICTED right to work (no expiration date)?
Rule / how to answer: If your work permit has an expiration date, the literal answer is No — read the definition in the question.

Question (common phrasing): Sponsorship question bundled with 'F-1 CPT letter / STEM OPT training plan'
Rule / how to answer: Answer truthfully. Treat the employer as HIGH sponsorship risk: ask the recruiter at first contact.

Question (common phrasing): Current visa type / status (free text or picker)
Rule / how to answer: Use the exact status you hold today (e.g. initial OPT vs STEM OPT extension are different).

Question (common phrasing): Work permit start/end dates (Format: MM/DD/YYYY to MM/DD/YYYY)
Rule / how to answer: Follow the stated format exactly; prose fails validation. If you don't have the dates yet, ask — never invent.

Question (common phrasing): Are you a U.S. citizen or permanent resident? / U.S. person?
Can you provide verification of identity and work eligibility (I-9) upon hire?
Can you work onsite at [location] N days/week?
Rule / how to answer: Decide per location BEFORE opening the form (some forms time out while you think).

Question (common phrasing): Are you open to relocation? / at your own expense?
Rule / how to answer: Relocation and in-office questions use DIFFERENT option wording on the same form — never copy one answer into the other.

Question (common phrasing): Do you live within N miles of [office]?
Rule / how to answer: Answer literally from your address.

Question (common phrasing): Desired salary / expected total compensation
Rule / how to answer: Set a rule once (e.g. 'midpoint of disclosed band, never below $X'). Check whether it asks BASE or TOTAL. Optional fields can stay blank.

Question (common phrasing): Do you accept the listed salary range?
Earliest start date / notice period
How did you hear about this job?
Rule / how to answer: Standing rule: pick the company career site option (it may be called Careers Page, Career Site, Company Website). If none exists, pick the closest honest option. On Workday this may be a multi-level menu.

Question (common phrasing): Were you referred? By whom?
Have you ever worked for [Company] or its subsidiaries (employee / contractor)?
Rule / how to answer: Answer from your timeline. Options are often full sentences, not Yes/No.

Question (common phrasing): Have you been employed by [audit firm, e.g. EY/PwC] within N months?
Rule / how to answer: Answer from your timeline.

Question (common phrasing): Are you bound by a non-compete / non-solicit with a former employer?
Were you a government employee in the last N years? (incl. public universities / state-owned entities)
Rule / how to answer: Definitions vary — some include publicly funded universities. Decide once, apply consistently.

Question (common phrasing): Do relatives or close friends work at [Company]?
Rule / how to answer: Ask EVERY time. Never reuse.

Question (common phrasing): Is a relative/close contact a government official (incl. state-owned enterprise employees)?
Rule / how to answer: Very broad definitions (can include public school teachers, state-owned bank staff). Ask every time.

Question (common phrasing): Outside business activities (advisory, board, side business) you'd continue?
Rule / how to answer: If your resume shows an ongoing side/volunteer role, answering No may contradict it.

Question (common phrasing): Is your current employer a customer/competitor of [Company]?
Citizen/resident of sanctioned countries (Cuba, Iran, N. Korea, Syria …)?
How many years of [X] experience do you have?
Rule / how to answer: Compute from the timeline; count only roles that honestly are X. Recruiters compare this with your resume dates.

Question (common phrasing): Rate your proficiency in Excel / SQL / Tableau …
Rule / how to answer: Use your Master Profile 1–5 ratings.

Question (common phrasing): Have you completed a Bachelor's / Master's degree?
Why do you want to work at [Company]? / What excites you about this role?
Rule / how to answer: Draft from one concrete product observation + one news item from the last 30 days. No mission-statement clichés. Show the user before submitting.

Question (common phrasing): What does our mission/purpose mean to you?
Rule / how to answer: Same approach; keep it specific.

Question (common phrasing): Tell us about yourself / summary (free text, e.g. Pinpoint 'summary')
Rule / how to answer: Optional but often the only free-text slot. Close on a positive note; don't concede gaps.

Question (common phrasing): Short essays (e.g. 'describe a model you built')
Rule / how to answer: Answer with a real project from the Bullet DB; honor any word limit.

Question (common phrasing): Which best describes how you use AI tools today? (ladder)
We may use AI to review applications — acknowledge
Rule / how to answer: User ticks.

Question (common phrasing): Do you consent to AI transcription/summary of interviews?
Pledge not to use AI tools during assessments/interviews
Rule / how to answer: A promise about how YOU will behave — always the user's call.

Question (common phrasing): Privacy notice / data processing acknowledgement
Rule / how to answer: User ticks. Claude never ticks legal boxes.

Question (common phrasing): Arbitration agreement / NDA acknowledgement / electronic signature
Rule / how to answer: User only. Some T&C boxes bundle an NDA — read before assuming it's just privacy.

Question (common phrasing): SMS / WhatsApp opt-in
Rule / how to answer: Options may be Opt-In/Opt-Out rather than Yes/No.

Question (common phrasing): Keep my data for future roles / join talent community
Rule / how to answer: Consider Yes at companies that cap applications per year — a recruiter contacting you doesn't count against the cap.

Question (common phrasing): Background check consent
Gender
Rule / how to answer: Option wording varies (Female / Woman / Cis-woman). Save your answer AND the decline wording; type a short filter and read the list before picking.

Question (common phrasing): Race / ethnicity (single or multi-select; may be granular)
Rule / how to answer: Some forms only show this after you answer Hispanic/Latino.

Question (common phrasing): Hispanic or Latino?
Veteran status
Rule / how to answer: Wording varies: 'I am not a protected veteran' vs 'I AM NOT A VETERAN'.

Question (common phrasing): Disability (CC-305)
Rule / how to answer: On Workday the CC-305 decline checkbox sometimes only registers when you click its text label.

Question (common phrasing): Sexual orientation / gender identity / LGBTQ+ / first-generation professional
Type your full legal name as signature / today's date
Rule / how to answer: Legal name. Date in the exact format requested.
